New Android Auto Update Is Bad News for Notifications, Version 18.1 Doesn't Help
6 photos
Photo: Google
If you need more proof that updating to a new Android Auto version on release date is not a good idea, here’s a notification bug that seems to be plaguing unlucky users who installed a recent update.
It’s all happening on devices running Android 17 and seemingly an Android Auto version newer than 17.9.
Someone on the Google forums says Android Auto 17.9 itself introduced this problem, but I was running version 18.0 when I first noticed it.
Due to this glitch, notifications no longer have sound on Android Auto, so while you might see the pop-up appearing on the screen, no audio goes through the car’s speakers. Oddly, it looks like Android Auto is actually trying to play the notification sound, as it pauses the music to play the notification sound, but no alert goes through the speakers.
The issue doesn’t appear very widespread at the moment, but users claim this is very new and only introduced by an update shipped this week. They point to version 17.9 as the most recently-installed Android Auto build - which makes sense, considering the rollout of this version in the stable channel is now supposed to reach broad availability - but the same thing seems to be happening on the newer 18.0 build.
The first thing that I tried was clearing the cache and the data in Android Auto because this workaround sometimes deals with small glitches like this one. It didn’t, and the notification sounds are still muted for Android Auto apps. I installed Android Auto 18.1 beta manually to see if the problem still occurs, and everything went back to normal on the first run.
The bug returned after I turned off the engine and disconnected the phone from my car, so eventually, version 18.1 did not help and seems to be suffering from the same glitch. Once I removed all Android Auto updates and started from scratch, everything went back to normal, but the notification sound bug reappeared once I updated to the latest version.
I run Android Auto with a Google Pixel 10 Pro XL and a factory-installed head unit with wireless support.
The only fix that I found, at least until Google comes up with a fix, is to remove all updates and block the automatic installation of new versions through the Google Play Store. Unfortunately, this could lead to other problems, as sticking with an older version means that you’re not getting the latest fixes and improvements, so you could end up hitting other bugs that have already been resolved.
A Google Community Specialist has already requested additional bug data on Google’s forums, and if you’re also battling this error, make sure you drop a comment in that thread.
